pre-fix-yarn.meaning: "Keepin' yer wits about ya on their tricks" changes staying informed into being alert, although all specific defensive steps and threats survive.
pre-fix-yarn.sense: "slanter websites" uses an obscure expression associated with a fraudulent trick/deal awkwardly as a website adjective; "swifties" otherwise fits.
pre-fix-yarn.authenticity: "handin'", "yer" and "yerself" are pushed through nearly every sentence, making the voice look performed rather than naturally broad.
pre-fix-yarn.register: "don't know from a bar of soap", "Shonks" and "cough up fees upfront" provide full level-5 body prose without demanding forbidden embellishment or swearing.
pre-fix-yarn.tone: "Government agencies will never ask ya for payment over the phone." retains the firm protective warning.
pre-fix-yarn.flow: "Dob in dodgy messages to the agency the scammer's tryin' to pass themselves off as" has a crowded join and repeated in/to construction.
pre-fix-yarn.variety: "swifties", "Shonks" and "Sting ya fees" offer variety, though "Dob in" repeats twice.
pre-fix-yarn.essence: "Always check the website URL ends in .gov." and the preserved scam-type headings keep the actionable guide’s shape.

dinkum-3.meaning: "Nine times outta ten" replaces often with a numerical frequency the original never claims; the remaining threats and protective instructions are retained.
dinkum-3.sense: "rorts" and "fair dinkum" correctly convey scams and legitimacy, and "on the spot" preserves immediacy.
dinkum-3.authenticity: "ya", "yer" and "yerself" recur almost everywhere, giving otherwise natural idiom a visibly performed quality.
dinkum-3.register: "gettin' onto the agency yerself", "give ya a ring" and "rorts goin' round" give sustained broad level-5 prose within the permitted vulgarity cap.
dinkum-3.tone: "Government agencies will never ask ya to pay over the phone." keeps the protective instruction firm.
dinkum-3.flow: "Hang up, then ring the official number" is crisp and easy to follow aloud.
dinkum-3.variety: "real deal", "fair dinkum" and "out of the blue" vary the language without a repeated decorative tag.
dinkum-3.essence: "type the official URL in yerself and double-check the spellin'" retains the guide’s concrete defensive steps and scam taxonomy.

current.meaning: "Demand that you cough up straightaway via gift cards, cryptocurrency, or wire transfers" preserves urgency and payment methods; all scam types and defences survive.
current.sense: "shonky websites", "Give search engines a miss" and "suss" all fit their intended meanings.
current.authenticity: "give you a ring" and "messages out of the blue" sound natural; dropped-g forms are present without dominating every word.
current.register: "Offer grants or financial assistance if you pay fees upfront" and other eligible bullets remain fairly neutral, so the overall voice is a little lighter than full level 5.
current.tone: "Government agencies will never ask you to pay over the phone." retains warning force and "Always check" remains mandatory.
current.flow: "Suss out whether the message is legit by gettin' in touch with the agency directly" reads cleanly and gives the user a clear action.
current.variety: "cough up", "shonky", "Give search engines a miss" and "out of the blue" vary the local language.
current.essence: "Report suss social media profiles to the social media platform." preserves the actionable educational character and the original progression.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: Keepin' yer wits about ya on their tricks is yer best defence.
pre-fix-yarn.original: Staying informed about these tactics is your best defense.
pre-fix-yarn.why: Being watchful is not quite the stated advice to remain informed about evolving tactics.
Slanter is an obscure trick/deal term and strains as an adjective for websites.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: handin' over their personal info or makin' dodgy payments
pre-fix-yarn.original: sharing their personal information or making fraudulent payments
pre-fix-yarn.why: Representative of pervasive eye dialect that gives the prose a performed sound rather than natural broad Australian speech.

pre-fix-yarn.quote: Dob in dodgy messages to the agency the scammer's tryin' to pass themselves off as
pre-fix-yarn.original: Report fraudulent messages to the agency the scammer is trying to represent
pre-fix-yarn.why: Crowded construction reads less cleanly than the surrounding instructions.
Repeats dob in as the stock reporting phrase.

dinkum-3.why: Invents an apparent nine-in-ten frequency; a quantitative-sounding claim is more specific than often.

dinkum-3.quote: handin' over yer personal info or makin' a dodgy payment
dinkum-3.original: sharing their personal information or making fraudulent payments
dinkum-3.why: Representative of pervasive eye dialect that makes the voice somewhat performed.

current.quote: Offer grants or financial assistance if you pay fees upfront
current.original: Offer grants or financial assistance in exchange for upfront fees
current.why: Representative of eligible body prose left relatively neutral, making the guide a shade lighter than requested level 5; protected technical terms need not be changed.

summaries.pre-fix-yarn: Complete practical advice in a very broad voice, weakened by eye dialect, an awkward term and one advice shift.
summaries.dinkum-3: Clear and broad, but invents a numerical frequency and leans heavily on eye dialect.
summaries.current: Most precise and natural, although the eligible prose is a little restrained for level 5.
